clue.text: Pianist going round the country, a star in the evenings

indicators.note: the pianist's name surrounds the country, its letters going round the outside

parts.note: Dame Myra Hess was a celebrated British concert pianist
Peru, the South American country

explanation.surface: A touring pianist, a star of the evening concert circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' is the container signal; 'Pianist going round the country' reads naturally as a concert tour. The evening star of classical verse is Venus seen at dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesperus is the classical name for Venus when it shines as the evening star after sunset.

clue.text: Going up in attack — daring act needs A line for power

indicators.note: line for power says L takes the place of P, the abbreviations for line and power

parts.note: an escapade is a daring or reckless adventure

explanation.surface: A daring stunt in an assault needs a line for extra power.
explanation.walkthrough: L (line) replaces P (power) in ESCAPADE. An escalade is the scaling of fortress walls with ladders, hence going up in attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Escalade is the military term for scaling a fortification's walls with ladders during an assault.

clue.text: Word for graphite? Exactly, in the past

parts.note: plumb as an adverb means exactly or precisely, as in plumb in the middle
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a term for pencil lead was exactly what was used long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Plumbago is another name for graphite, from the Latin for lead-like ore.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbago is an older name for graphite, the black carbon used in pencils.

clue.text: Ready to turn haunt upside down

indicators.note: in a down light, upside down means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a lair is a haunt or den

explanation.surface: Something is ready to turn a ghost's haunt upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upside down' reverses LAIR. Ready is slang for cash, and the rial is a currency of Iran and Oman.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready means ready money or cash, and the rial is a monetary unit in several Middle Eastern countries.

clue.text: Environment for making up a crossword puzzle

definitions.meaning: the surroundings or backdrop in which something takes place
the compiler's act of composing the grid and its clues

explanation.surface: Someone describes the backdrop for compiling a crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is only a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A setting is a backdrop or surroundings, and compilers are said to set the puzzles they make.

clue.text: Sailor impish and mad disciplined before head of Navy

indicators.note: before says the scrambled letters come ahead of the next piece
disciplined means knocked into shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A mischievous, unruly sailor is brought into line before the head of the Navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disciplined' scrambles IMPISH and MAD (the 'and' is a link), and 'head of' gives N from Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A midshipman is a junior naval officer, so a kind of sailor.

clue.text: Artist outside more when it's dry

clue.text: Heartless bloke's share in the action of twisters

indicators.note: Heartless says the middle letter of the word is taken out

parts.note: guy is an informal word for a bloke
a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: A callous man's portion in the spinning of tornadoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' takes the U from GUY, leaving GY; 'in' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyration is spinning motion, which is what whirlwinds and twisters do.

clue.text: English girl, 21, knocking one out — I'm sent!

parts.note: miss, a young unmarried woman

indicators.note: knocking one out says a single letter is struck from the cross-referenced word

parts.note: refers to the answer at 21 across, a word meaning nonchalant
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An English girl, breezy and carefree, announces with delight that she is thrilled to bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking ... out' removes I from AIRY (the answer to 21 across), leaving ARY. 'I'm sent!' reads as excitement, but in the sense of dispatched it defines an envoy speaking for herself.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy is someone dispatched on a mission, so the clue's speaker saying they are sent describes themselves.

clue.text: In a month, trophy goes to a new holder

indicators.note: In says the following pieces sit inside the abbreviated month

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October
a cup is a sporting trophy

explanation.surface: A sports trophy changes hands within the month, passing to its next holder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the container signal and 'goes to' is only a link; the surface sounds like a trophy changing hands, while 'holder' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An occupant holds a place or position, so a holder of a post or tenancy is its occupant.

clue.text: Island that volunteer force raves about?

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force; with the possessive it gives TA'S
a mania is something people rave about, a craze

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the reserve soldiers are so enthusiastic about.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve; the question mark flags the whimsical reading of the island as what that force is crazy about.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania is the large island state lying south of mainland Australia.

clue.text: In April, a wind devastated Pakistani city

indicators.note: devastated means wrecked, so the letters of the preceding words are wrecked and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spring gale wrecks a city in Pakistan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devastated' scrambles APRIL A WIND; 'In' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rawalpindi is a major city in the Punjab province of Pakistan, beside the capital Islamabad.

clue.text: A short distance inside the factory there's unison singing

indicators.note: inside says the small measure goes into the factory word

parts.note: a plant is a factory
an inch is a short distance

explanation.surface: In the works, only a short way in, workers are singing in unison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' is the container signal and 'there's' only a link; 'A short distance' supplies two pieces, the article as written plus the measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainchant is unaccompanied church music sung in unison in a single melodic line.

clue.text: Priest starts to lead evensong at six

indicators.note: starts to says take the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A clergyman begins to lead the evening service at six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes L and E from 'lead' and 'evensong'.
explanation.definitionFit: Levi was the founder of the Levites, the Israelite tribe set apart for priestly duties, so the name stands for a priest.

clue.text: Judge from York had returned on circuit

indicators.note: on circuit says the turned letters run round the outside of the city's old name
returned means the word had is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: Ebor is the traditional short form of York's Latin name, Eboracum, used in church signatures and horse racing

explanation.surface: A judge from York has come back from travelling the court circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' gives DAH and 'on circuit' wraps it round the old name of York. The judge is the biblical one; English judges travel on circuit, which disguises the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Deborah was a prophetess who served as one of the Judges of Israel in the Old Testament Book of Judges.

clue.text: Works in a surprise attack set up to get people dispersing

indicators.note: in a down entry set up means the assembled letters are read upwards
in says the works go inside the attack

parts.note: a raid is a surprise attack
ops, short for opera, is a plural of opus, a work

explanation.surface: Operations within a raid are arranged to scatter the population.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' builds AROPSAID and 'set up' turns it upwards, as befits a down entry. Ops is the plural of opus, a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaspora is a scattering of a people away from their homeland.

clue.text: One's grub is stewed mushrooms

indicators.note: stewed signals the letters are cooked up into a new order

parts.note: the 's gives an S, so One's provides ONES
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's food turns out to be stewed fungi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stewed' scrambles ONES and GRUB; 'mushrooms' is a verb, not food.
explanation.definitionFit: To mushroom is to spring up and grow fast, which is what something that burgeons does.

clue.text: Monarch adopts this writer? Boy, he could write!

indicators.note: adopts means takes in, so the monarch's letters take in the setter's pronoun

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the monarch's cipher
this writer refers to the setter, giving me
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A monarch adopts a boy who turns out to be a gifted writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopts' is the container signal. Ralph Waldo Emerson, the American essayist, is the writer meant; 'this writer' is the setter speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was a celebrated American essayist and poet, so he was indeed someone who could write.

clue.text: A Doctor that's moved heavenward? This saint, maybe

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification
rose is the past tense of rise, to move upward

explanation.surface: A doctor who has gone to heaven might be this saint.
explanation.walkthrough: St Ambrose was a fourth-century Bishop of Milan and Doctor of the Church, which the surface hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrose is a well-known saint, the fourth-century Bishop of Milan.

clue.text: Brownie? Not female to be nonchalant

indicators.note: Not female says the female abbreviation is taken away from the sprite

parts.note: a brownie is a helpful household sprite of folklore, a kind of fairy; the question mark marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A girl in the junior Guides is told not to be so casual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' drops F from FAIRY. A Brownie is also a junior Girl Guide, which makes 'female' look natural.
explanation.definitionFit: An airy manner is light and casual, a synonym for nonchalant.

clue.text: Only women left in desert that was fought over

definitions.text: Only women left in desert that was fought over

parts.words: Only women left in desert that was fought over
parts.note: a stretch of wasteland where no men remain, which is also the contested ground between opposing trench lines

explanation.surface: With the men gone, only women remain on the barren battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads both as a place with no males left and as the empty ground between front lines that both sides contested.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the unoccupied strip between opposing armies' trenches, deserted and fought over in the First World War.

clue.text: He may drone on — one feeling pained in advance?

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before or in advance
an acher is someone who aches

explanation.surface: A sufferer in pain complains in advance that someone will drone on.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the stereotype of a dull sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: A tedious minister sermonizing at length is the stock figure who may drone on from the pulpit.

clue.text: Producer of engines needing excessive oxygen

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means excessive
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An engine maker needs more than enough oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: Nikolaus Otto built the first four-stroke internal combustion engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikolaus Otto was the German engineer who developed the four-stroke internal combustion engine.

clue.text: Foreigner finding our diet's terrible

indicators.note: terrible signals that the letters are wrecked and remade

parts.note: the 's here gives an S, so diet's provides DIETS

explanation.surface: A foreigner discovers that our food is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' scrambles OUR and DIETS; 'finding' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An outsider is someone who does not belong, which is what a foreigner is in a strange country.

clue.text: Managed to be alongside rulers in hierarchical scale

definitions.note: the plural answer names the ordered list as a whole

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it, past tense ran
kings are rulers

explanation.surface: Someone managed to rub shoulders with royalty in the social pecking order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be alongside' only joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Rankings are an ordered list placing people or teams by position, which is a scale of hierarchy.

clue.text: Stretch alone — get disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed means upset and rearranged, so the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone told to go off alone gets upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' scrambles ALONE and GET.
explanation.definitionFit: To elongate is to make longer, a synonym for stretch as a verb.
